settings.updateAvailableDismissed: Running version {version}. Version {latest} is available. You've dismissed the notice for it. Last checked {checked}.
settings.updateCurrent: Running version {version} — up to date. Last checked {checked}.
settings.updateCurrentStale: Running version {version} — up to date. Last checked {checked}. The most recent attempt failed.
settings.dataRetentionDescription: When on, an archived competition is permanently deleted — database records and stored files — once it has stayed archived for the retention period. The archive dialog shows the exact deletion date; unarchiving cancels the clock. Competitions archived before enabling this are never auto-deleted.
settings.autoDeleteOn: On — delete after the retention period
settings.emailAllowlistDescription: Restrict public sign-up to specific email domains. A rejected sign-up sees a generic error — it never learns which domains are allowed. Applies to public registration only; admin-created accounts and existing users' emails are unaffected. Enabling this makes email mandatory at registration.
settings.allowlistOn: On — only allowed domains may register
settings.emailVerificationDescription: Require a self-registered account to confirm its email (a link sent via the SMTP server below) before it can join a competition. Requires SMTP to be configured. Admin-created accounts (Admin → Users) are exempt, and turning this on never affects members who already joined.
settings.verificationOff: Off — anyone who registers can join
settings.smtpDescription: Used by the automation <mono>send_email</mono> action. Leave the host blank to disable email (the action becomes a no-op).
settings.subdomainsHint: Subdomains are automatically allowed (e.g. an entry for <mono>example.com</mono> also allows <mono>mail.example.com</mono>).

rules.title: Rules / code of conduct
rules.description: Shown to users before they join any competition. Unless display-only is on, joining requires an explicit “I accept”. A competition can supersede this with its own override (Competition Settings → Rules). Leave empty for no rules and no prompt.
rules.displayOnlyHint: — show the rules at join without requiring acceptance.

backup.exportDescription: Download a backup of the selected data as a JSON file. Includes secrets (password & flag hashes, SMTP credentials) — store it securely.
backup.importDescription: Restore from an export file. Additive — it adds records that don't already exist and never overwrites or deletes current data. Existing competitions (matched by name) and users (by name/email) are skipped.
backup.importConfirmDescription: New records from the selected sections are added to this platform. Existing data is never overwritten or deleted, but this can't be undone selectively.
backup.importedToast: Imported {count, plural, one {# record} other {# records}}

apiTokens.heading: API tokens
apiTokens.headingDescription: Every token on the platform. Users create their own from their profile; you can revoke any of them here.
apiTokens.noTokensDescription: Nobody has created a personal API token yet.
apiTokens.revokeDescription: {description} (held by {holder}) will stop authenticating immediately. This can't be undone.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: Palette controls surface colours; accent controls action colours. Mix freely.
appearance.platformNameHint: Shown in the sidebar, on the sign-in screen, and in the browser tab.
appearance.backgroundDescription: An animated backdrop for the sign-in, registration and public pages. It uses your accent colour, and only shows on dark palettes.
appearance.lightPaletteWarning: The current palette is light, so this background won't show — animated backgrounds are shown on dark palettes only.
appearance.noticeDescription: Shown above the sign-in card — event instructions, which account to use, who to contact. Visible to anyone who can reach the sign-in page, so keep it public information. Delete all the text to remove the notice.
appearance.logoDescription: Replace the built-in mark with your organisation's logo. Shown in the sidebar and on the sign-in screen. PNG, SVG, WebP or GIF, up to 1 MB — a transparent background that reads on a dark ground works best. Flagpost stays credited via the “Powered by Flagpost” footer regardless.
appearance.showWordmark: Show the platform name beside the logo
appearance.showWordmarkHint: (turn off if your logo already includes your name)
appearance.removeLogoDescription: The built-in Flagpost mark will be shown instead.

ai.providerDescription: Point Flagpost at any OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint — a hosted API or a local model (Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio). The model must support tool calling; the assistant answers entirely through read-only tools. The base URL is a trusted operator setting, so it is not subject to the outbound-request blocklist a local address needs.
ai.removeStoredKey: Remove the stored key (use a keyless endpoint)
ai.keyNotSet: Not set — leave blank for a keyless endpoint
ai.responseLimitsDescription: Caps that bound each answer's length and how long Flagpost waits on the provider — the guardrails against a slow endpoint or a runaway token bill.
ai.adminPromptDescription: An optional override for the assistant's system prompt. It governs tone and focus only — the assistant is read-only and every tool re-checks your permissions, so no wording can widen what it can see. Leave blank to use the built-in prompt.
ai.testSaveFirst: Save a base URL and model first
ai.setBeforeEnabling: Set a base URL and model before enabling the AI module
